Task id: t01_slugify

# Issue #41: `slugify` produces double hyphens and trailing hyphens

`slugify("Hello,  World!")` returns `"hello--world-"` but should return `"hello-world"`.
Also `slugify("--a--b--")` should give `"a-b"`.

Please fix `textkit/slug.py`. Do not change the public signature.


Repository files:
tests/test_slug.py
textkit/__init__.py
textkit/slug.py

1| import re
   2| 
   3| def slugify(text: str) -> str:
   4|     """Turn arbitrary text into a URL slug: lowercase, ASCII letters and
   5|     digits, words separated by single hyphens, no leading/trailing hyphens."""
   6|     text = text.lower()
   7|     text = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "-", text)
   8|     return text

1| import unittest
   2| from textkit import slugify
   3| 
   4| class TestSlug(unittest.TestCase):
   5|     def test_basic(self):
   6|         self.assertEqual(slugify("Hello World"), "hello-world")
   7|     def test_punct(self):
   8|         self.assertEqual(slugify("Hello,  World!"), "hello-world")
   9| 
  10| if __name__ == "__main__":
  11|     unittest.main()

The bug is clear: the regex `[^a-z0-9]` replaces each non-alphanumeric character individually with a hyphen, so consecutive characters produce consecutive hyphens, and leading/trailing characters produce leading/trailing hyphens. Fix: use `+` to collapse runs, and strip the ends.

1| import re
   2| 
   3| def slugify(text: str) -> str:
   4|     """Turn arbitrary text into a URL slug: lowercase, ASCII letters and
   5|     digits, words separated by single hyphens, no leading/trailing hyphens."""
   6|     text = text.lower()
   7|     text = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", text)
   8|     return text.strip("-")

The fix is verified against all cases:

- `slugify("Hello,  World!")` → `"hello,  world!"` → `"hello-world-"` → `"hello-world"` ✓
- `slugify("--a--b--")` → `"-a-b-"` → `"a-b"` ✓
- `slugify("Hello World")` → `"hello-world"` ✓ (existing test still passes)

The change is minimal: `[^a-z0-9]+` collapses runs of non-alphanumeric characters into a single hyphen, and `.strip("-")` removes any leading/trailing hyphens. The public signature is unchanged.

arguments.summary: Fixed `slugify` in textkit/slug.py by changing the regex from `[^a-z0-9]` to `[^a-z0-9]+` so consecutive non-alphanumeric characters collapse into a single hyphen, and added `.strip("-")` to remove leading/trailing hyphens. This makes `slugify("Hello,  World!")` return `"hello-world"` and `slugify("--a--b--")` return `"a-b"`, while keeping the public signature unchanged.
